verdicts.title: Fail-closed is the shipped default and the Weather Safety page never tells a sensorless rig what that means
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end on a fresh v-misc profile with nothing connected. (1) Default verified two ways: app_settings.dart:82 is `@Default(SafetyFailMode.failClosed) SafetyFailMode safetyFailMode` and the fresh scratch DB row reads `safety_fail_mode|failClosed`. (2) 'Enable weather safety' does default OFF -- weather_settings.dart:48 `@Default(false)` and weather_settings_dao.dart:33/150 explicitly insert `weatherSafetyEnabled: const Value(false)`; the live page rendered the switch off. (3) The Weather Safety page really is only 3 toggles + 3 thresholds + 2 alert-timing numbers: the AT-SPI tree of the live page lists exactly Enable weather safety / Auto-park mount / Auto-resume after clear / Max humidity / Max wind speed / Max cloud cover / Alert distance / Lead time and nothing else. No source row, no fail-mode control, no count of attached weather devices -- confirmed against the full 268-line widget source as well. (4) The fail-mode selector really is on another page: `safetyFailMode` appears in exactly one app file, sequencer_settings.dart:569-572, and typing 'Safety fail' into the live Settings search returns a single hit, 'Sequencer'. (5) The consequence reproduces immediately: toggling 'Enable weather safety' on with no weather device and no safety monitor fired a CRITICAL notification within seconds -- title 'Safe the rig', body 'CRITICAL: No weather data sources available. Rig safed: no action was possible. NO MOUNT CONNECTED - nothing was parked; if a mount is tracking under another program it is still exposed.' The Rust log shows 'Secondary rig stopped' at the same instant, i.e. SafeRigService actually executed. Cited file:line is accurate (weather_safety_settings.dart:123-175 is the SettingsPage / Safety Actions block, master switch at 133-143; weather_safety_rules.dart is 72 lines and the rule spans essentially all of it). Severity corrected P1 -> P2 because the finding's framing ('invisible until it fires', 'the run will park and abort shortly after it starts') overstates what ships today: WeatherSafetyNoSourceRule is registered in the pre-flight validator (sequence_validation.dart:348) at ValidationSeverity.error, and every start path throws SequenceValidationException when any error-severity issue is present (sequence_validation.dart:474-493), so this configuration BLOCKS the run before it starts rather than aborting it after a slew, and the thrown message carries the resolution hint naming Settings > Automation & Safety. That plus the master switch defaulting off and the loud CRITICAL toast the instant it is switched on means the operator is not silently doomed. What remains, and is genuinely wrong, is that the page owning the master switch discloses neither the fail mode nor the absence of sources, and the CRITICAL toast itself never says 'fail mode' or where to change it. Real disclosure defect, not a night-loss P1.

verdicts.title: PHD2 Guiding settings has no way to test the connection -- the one integration you cannot verify
verdicts.location_wrong: File is right (phd2_guiding_settings.dart, all 209 lines) but the finding's list of what is missing is wrong in two places -- 'no live PHD2 connection state' and 'no launch PHD2 if not running' both exist in the app, on the Guiding screen. A fixer acting on the finding as written would rebuild Phd2Launcher and the onboarding tester.
verdicts.reasoning: The literal claim reproduces. Live AT-SPI tree of Settings > PHD2 Guiding lists exactly: Host, Port, PHD2 executable path ('Auto-detect (optional)' / 'Not set'), and the Information paragraph. No Test/Connect button, no connection state, no version, no profile selector -- matching the full 209-line source. The 'Not set' subtitle is only a reflection of an empty phd2Path, not a probe result, so the contrast with Plate Solving is fair: plate_solving_settings_screen.dart:390/403/441 really do render 'Auto-detect - not found' from a live detection, and Send test / Test Connection really do exist in transport_controls.dart and cloud_sync_settings.dart. BUT the finding's headline rationale -- 'the one integration you cannot verify', 'the only one with no verification affordance' -- is false, and I refuted it in the running app rather than on paper. (a) The Guiding screen header shows live 'PHD2 Disconnected' with a Connect button; I clicked it and the app raised a toast titled 'PHD2' reading 'PHD2 not running - searching for installed PHD2...' -- that string is phd2_launcher.dart:99, and Phd2Launcher does exactly the thing the finding says does not exist: launches the configured executable (or calls apiLaunchPhd2 when the path is blank), then polls host:port until it opens, with distinct errors for 'executable not found', 'failed to launch' and 'launched but did not open port'. So PHD2 reachability IS testable from the app, with real diagnostics. (b) Onboarding > Guider already has the exact affordance the finding asks for: a 'Test' button calling GuidingBackend.isPhd2Running(host, port) that renders 'PHD2 reachable at <host:port>. Selection saved.' or 'No response on <host:port>. Is PHD2 running with "Enable Server" turned on?' (guider_step.dart:73-121 and 234-245), and persists phd2Host/phd2Port on success. Two sub-claims survive: there is no PHD2 version readout anywhere, and no profile selector -- the bridge does expose api_phd2_get_profile (phd2.rs:749) but apiPhd2GetProfile has zero Dart callers outside the generated binding, so that is dead capability rather than shipped UI. Severity corrected P1 -> P3: this is a parity/discoverability gap on one settings page for a capability that already exists two clicks away, not an unverifiable integration and not a risk to an observing night. Not a duplicate of the other finding in this batch (different unit, different page).
